claims.text: The initial FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a 15–45 μm particle-size distribution.
Standard HVAF-i7 settings with 15–45 μm feedstock produce acceptable-quality coatings but inadequate thickness.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to approximately 350 mm increases in-flight particle velocity.
Higher particle velocity increases the particles' in-flight kinetic energy.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy improves splat formation and flattening on impact.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy improves inter-splat bonding and adhesion.
Improved impact behavior raises the deposition efficiency or deposition rate.
The higher deposition efficiency produces a thicker FeCoNiCrAl coating.
Low-temperature HVAF-i7 processing minimizes oxidation despite increased particle speed.
Spraying at approximately 350 mm will produce a thicker, adherent bond coat with minimal as-sprayed oxidation relative to the standard HVAF-i7 baseline.
The resulting coating quality will match or exceed the benchmark established by HVAF-M3 spraying with 15–45 μm feedstock.
The intervention remains effective under low-temperature deposition conditions and at spray distances from 300 to 350 mm.
The proposed HVAF-i7 process is applicable to internal geometries with diameters as small as 120 mm.
Departures from the stated low-temperature and 300–350 mm operating window may compromise coating integrity or oxidation control.
